classification.difficultyReason: Requires constructing the triangle of centres and subtracting three sectors from its area.

inlines.text: Find the area bounded by the three minor arcs ending at the points of contact.

spec.description: Three equal externally tangent circles, one above two lower circles. The central curved triangular gap is shaded. Only the lower-left centre is marked, with a radius labelled r directed upwards and rightwards.
spec.mathematics: Equal radii and external tangency place the centres at the vertices of an equilateral triangle of side 2r. The target boundary consists of three minor arcs of central angle π/3. The displayed radius follows the source orientation and is not a triangle-of-centres construction.
spec.answerVisibility: The source radius and target region are visible; centre joins, sector angles and the requested area are not supplied.

answer.short:
$\left(\sqrt3-\dfrac{\pi}{2}\right)r^2$.

Join the centres to form an equilateral triangle of side $2r$, then subtract the three $\frac{\pi}{3}$ sectors.
answer.worked:
Join the three centres. They form an equilateral triangle of side $2r$, so each angle is $\frac{\pi}{3}$.

Its area is
$$\begin{align*}
T&=\frac12(2r)(2r)\sin\frac{\pi}{3}\\
T&=\sqrt3\,r^2.
\end{align*}$$
Subtract the three sectors inside the triangle:
$$\begin{align*}
A&=\sqrt3\,r^2-3\left(\frac12r^2\frac{\pi}{3}\right)\\
A&=\left(\sqrt3-\frac{\pi}{2}\right)r^2.
\end{align*}$$
